segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus:
he was asking news of his sons and of his eldest son, the one who had imprisoned him.
They said to him,
"Do you want to eat? Do you want to drink? Beyond this, do not ask us anything."
It is said
that when they were bringing him across the bridge,
then he awoke,
and he saw the Tigris and said,
"Do you wish to drown me?" But they replied,
"No,
rather we are taking you to Kawashi."
And he said,
"This was in my mind,
that is, to imprison my son there;
but he has anticipated me in doing it."
And this Abu Taghlib undertook to send to Baghdad the tribute that his father used to send,
and 'Izz al-Dawlah, the emir of Baghdad, made peace with him.
And in the place of Sayf al-Dawlah, the emir of Aleppo and of Homs, his son Abu'l-Ma'ali sat.
And in the year one thousand two hundred and seventy-nine
[1279] of the Greeks,
which is the year 357
[357] of the Arabs,
certain Khurasanians together with three thousand Arabs, the people of Antioch, campaigned into the country of Cappadocia.
And forty thousand Romans met them,
and they killed the majority of the Khurasanians and the people of Antioch,
and they captured many of them.
And the Arabs who were in Antioch killed the patriarch of the Chalcedonians,
and they destroyed most of the churches of Antioch.
And the Romans went out again to Sarug,
and they captured three hundred Arabs and much cattle,
and they departed.
And in the same year Nasir al-Dawlah died in the prison of Kawashi,
and he was brought to the Hill of Repentance opposite Mosul,
and he was buried there;
and all his sons walked with their swords drawn before his bier.
In this year, when Abu'l-'Ala Sulayman bar Wahb bar Sufyan, a Christian notary of Baghdad, was found to have three hundred and fifty thousand zuzes with a certain banker,
and twelve thousand casks of wine in his house,
they fined him one hundred and forty thousand white pieces and let him go.
And in this year,
division fell between the Khurasanians who were in Antioch and the Arabs, the people of Antioch.
And the Romans came and took captive from the region of Antioch twelve thousand people:
men and women, boys and girls.
And after a year, that is in the year one thousand two hundred and eighty
[1280] of the Greeks
([969] of our Lord?),
the Romans came to Kfartuta,
and they carried off eight hundred people from it, along with much plunder.
